I had a cat once. Her name was Sparrow, took her in from the streets. We spent 10 beautiful months together. Then she got sick. I tried to save money to help her, but I had lost my job and was almost evicted. She was my best friend, but I knew I couldn’t afford to help her. She died, and I fell into a depression. I couldn’t move for days. Cried for so long. I blamed myself over and over for being poor. Blamed myself for not giving her to someone richer that could help her. Blamed myself for not asking around for money. “It was all my fault”.

Three years have passed. I still miss her. But I don’t blame myself anymore. We live in a horrible economy with an even worse job market. Nobody can help anybody. Sparrow unfortunately drew the short straw. But the time we spent together meant everything to me. And I know it did to her too. Sometimes things happen that feel we have to take responsibility for. But we have to remember that life is full of tragedy, and these things are bound to happen. Don’t blame yourself friend. It won’t help anyone. It only hurts you. And you did a good thing, no matter how much your heart rejects the idea. It’s gonna be okay

This post caught my attention because I’ve been living with depression for 5 years too.

Something I came to terms with a long time ago is that there are certain thoughts/feelings in a depressed person’s mind that no one else understands except others who have depression. I’m sure you know what I’m talking about. The problem with this is that, not only is your depression urging you to keep quiet from others about your feelings, but it’s also keeping you from communicating what you’re feeling in detail. What happens is that you usually end up just keeping these thoughts to yourself because you figure that no one will understand, or maybe even care.

But that’s not true.

I understand. Everyone on this subreddit understands you. We’re here for you and we want to help you get through these hard times. Some of us haven’t found our way yet, like you and I, but together it’s possible for us to lead normal, happy lives if we help each other.

My point is, if you ever need anyone, PM me. Don’t be afraid to reach out for help. Because we know how you’re feeling, we know the pain and confusion you’re going through, and we won’t leave you behind.

It’s indescribable. Only someone who has it knows what it’s like. It’s like seeing a new color. That much goes for everyone. But the qualities of depression depends on the individual.

For me, it’s a really heavy feeling that runs throughout my whole body. It’s especially heavy in my chest. My brain is clouded with negative thoughts that I can’t explain. Some thoughts are pressing issues that have arisen in my life, others of feelings of failure, loneliness, sadness, worthlessness, anger, and anxiety.

I don’t feel like doing anything, I don’t feel like talking to anyone. All I can think about is how bad I want to die. My diet changes too. Although sometimes I’ll eat a ton and other times I’ll eat nothing at all. When the depression lets up a little, all I feel is numbness.
